judge_assessment.explanation: Every comparison the judge names is correct and I re-derived all sixteen checks independently: 462>429, 352>328 from Ella's 3/5/2 and Ryan's 3/2/8 blocks, 508<580, 615<651, the ascending 437/473/743, 209>198 from Sam's 2/0/9 and Nina's 1/9/8, 384<389, 892<928, the descending 650/605/560, and problem 10's 557 as the only 5_7 value strictly between 547 and 587 once the tens digit is minimised. The judge's OCR explanation for the count warning is also right -- there are exactly ten \problem bodies. But instruction_following 4 is not supportable. The task prompt says 'clearly label any genuinely open response for manual review', and final_response.md claims '**Nothing is flagged for manual review** -- the build finished with every gate green.' Problem 6 says 'compare them with > or <, and explain in one sentence', and problem 8 says 'Is Maya right? Compare the two numbers with > or < and explain which place you looked at first.' Neither carries a manual entry; verify.json records both as compare only, and the machine observation duly reports gate_chain_manual_flags: false. The delivered summary therefore asserts complete machine coverage of a sheet that asks for two written explanations. Separately the Quick Answers bank prints '-' in seven of ten rows (1, 3, 4, 7, 8 entirely; 2, 6, 10 partially) on a sheet with ZERO manual items -- every one of those dashes is a verified relation that render_quick_answers refused to typeset.

strengths_to_preserve: Problem 6 (Sam: 2 flats, 0 rods, 9 cubes vs Nina: 1 flat, 9 rods, 8 cubes) attacks the 'more rods must mean more' misconception head-on inside a representations sheet, and the declared trap -- reading Sam's blocks as 29 by skipping the empty tens place -- is machine-proved distinct from 209.

The place-value chart is redrawn inside problems 1, 3, 7 and 10 rather than referenced once, so the child fills a fresh chart each time and the method the directions teach is actually exercised on the page.

Problem 10 is a real construction task rather than another comparison: the tens digit is blank in the chart and the number must beat two tests at once ('greater than 547 and less than 587'), with both bounds verified as separate compare entries (557 > 547 and 557 < 587).

root_causes.description: Nothing forces an explanation prompt to produce a manual entry, so a worksheet can print 'explain in one sentence' twice and still report zero manual flags. The delivery summary then repeats that as a claim of complete verification.
evidence: worksheet.tex problem 6: '... compare them with $>$ or $<$, and explain in one sentence.' Problem 8: '... explain which place you looked at first.'
verify.json has only compare entries for ids 6 and 8; no manual entry exists anywhere in the file.
final_response.md: '**Nothing is flagged for manual review** -- the build finished with every gate green.'
SKILL.md already directs authors to use manual for any explanation or reasoning answer, so the guidance exists but is unenforced.

root_causes.description: render_quick_answers._fmt sends relation strings through bare sympy.sympify, which raises, and falls back to '---'. On a comparison worksheet that is most of the bank, and here it is worse than ambiguous -- there are no manual items at all, so the dashes are pure loss.
evidence: verify.json contains no manual entries; every dashed value is a compare/relation expected that PASSED.
The key body prints the relations in full (e.g. '462 > 429'), so the data exists and only the bank loses it.

root_causes.description: Coverage is per problem id, so problems that print an extra response slot beyond the comparison satisfy the gate with one entry.
evidence: Problem 3: 'Which place decides the answer? Write it on your work space.' -- the answer 'tens' has no entry.
Problem 4: '... then write the name of the school that collected more' -- 'Pine School' has no entry.
Problem 8: 'Is Maya right?' -- the yes/no judgement has no entry.

improvements.title: Stop reporting zero manual items on a sheet that asks twice for a written explanation
improvements.proposed_change: Add a gate that scans each \problem body for explanation cues ('explain', 'tell how you know', 'say in one sentence', 'why', 'describe') and fails unless that problem id carries a manual entry in addition to its machine checks. Then derive the manual-review sentence in the delivery summary from verify.json rather than from author prose, so 'Nothing is flagged for manual review' cannot be written while problems 6 and 8 demand sentences.
improvements.regression_test: Fixture whose problem text contains 'explain in one sentence' while its only entry is a compare: the gate must exit non-zero naming the id. Today the fixture builds green (curr-053 did, with gate_chain_manual_flags false); after the fix it fails, and the variant carrying a manual entry passes and reports one manual item.
improvements.expected_impact: Removes false claims of complete machine coverage -- the failure mode most damaging to trust in the materials -- and gets grading guidance attached to the explanations a teacher actually has to read.
improvements.risk: Cue-word matching will over-trigger on stems that merely narrate an explanation; scope it to imperative sentences inside \problem bodies with an explicit author override.

improvements.title: Typeset verified comparison relations in the Quick Answers bank
improvements.proposed_change: Special-case relation strings in scripts/render_quick_answers.py._fmt before the sympify call, rendering them with the compared 'values' (e.g. '$462 > 429$'), and give manual-only rows a distinct marker. On this sheet that converts seven dashed rows into complete answers.
improvements.regression_test: tests/test_render_quick_answers.py: a compare/relation entry must render the relation and never '---'; a manual-only entry must render a distinct marker. Fails today, passes after.
improvements.expected_impact: A comparison-focused worksheet gets a usable quick-check strip instead of a column of dashes.
improvements.risk: Longer entries reduce the bank's column count; verify the answer key still fits its page budget.

improvements.title: Cover the extra response slots in problems 3, 4 and 8
improvements.proposed_change: Make the SKILL.md coverage rule slot-level and enforce it in tests/check_layout.py by counting rendered answer-location macros per \problem against the expecteds bound to that id. Here that requires entries for 'which place decides the answer' (tens), the school name in problem 4 (Pine School), and the yes/no judgement in problem 8 -- all expressible as read_data lookups.
improvements.regression_test: Fixture printing a comparison slot plus a named-answer slot with a single compare entry: check_layout must exit non-zero. Passes today, fails after until the second entry is added.
improvements.expected_impact: The answer a story problem actually asks for ('which school collected more') stops being unverified while its numeric proxy is checked.
improvements.risk: Requires back-filling existing verify files; the slot counter must ignore decorative rules.

case_summary: Mathematically flawless -- all sixteen checks recomputed correct, including 557 as the unique minimal solution to the two-sided constraint in problem 10 -- and the representations are meaningful rather than decorative, with base-ten blocks, charts and story counts all feeding the same place-by-place method. The problems are correctly ordered by difficulty and never require arithmetic beyond place value. What the 32/32 does not capture: the sheet asks for two written explanations (problems 6 and 8) and reports zero manual items, with final_response.md stating outright that nothing is flagged for manual review; the Quick Answers bank prints dashes on seven of ten rows despite there being no manual items at all; and three problems print a response slot (which place, which school, is Maya right) that no verify entry covers.
